A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LarPO study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–H are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original LarPO evaluations and ablations in Sections 5–6, plus original SFT/DPO and retrieval experiments in the appendices. Some baseline scores are explicitly attributed to prior work.

after.justification: V2 retains the original evaluations and analyses, including the LarPO benchmark results and Appendix B's SFT/DPO experiments.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4, Table 1 and Algorithm 1 retain the same LarPO objectives, iterative training procedure, hard-negative selection and candidate reuse. The rewritten conclusion does not change the documented method.

E1.justification: The training and evaluation coverage is unchanged, including UltraFeedback, MetaMath, AlpacaEval2, MixEval/MixEval-Hard, GSM8K, MATH and NQ. The removed RAG conclusion has no corresponding experimental coverage elsewhere in either PDF.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains SFT, RRHF, SLiC-HF, DPO, IPO, CPO, KTO, RDPO, SimPO and iterative DPO in the same comparison groups. Comparator membership in the supplementary studies also matches.

E3.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendix H preserve the same splits, model configurations, evaluation metrics and evaluators, training budgets, response counts, temperatures and checkpoint-selection procedures.

E4.justification: The objective, negative-hardness, temperature and candidate-list studies are unchanged. Appendices B and E retain the same SFT/DPO and retrieval analyses, and Appendix H retains the supplementary temperature study.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting, without reported random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 removes Section 8's qualitative statement that RAG performance first improves and then degrades as more passages are included; neither PDF provides a corresponding RAG experiment. All tabulated and plotted experimental results, including Tables 2–4 and 6–7 and Figures 2 and 4–6, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The IR/LLM definitions, ranking assumptions, mathematical derivations and Theorems F.1–F.3 with their proofs remain identical.

C1.justification: Section 8 replaces claims about a long-context RAG study and three RAG remedies with a summary of the IR-alignment framework and LarPO. This corrects the conclusion to match the existing work; the abstract and introduction's core contributions and claimed improvements remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 removes the misplaced conclusion's attribution of RAG degradation to retrieved hard negatives and its RAG-focused future directions. The LarPO interpretations, temperature/diversity caveats and qualifications of the IR analogy elsewhere remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix H retains identical hyperparameters, response-construction rules, checkpoint-selection details and evaluator identifiers. Implementation and code/data access information do not change.

R1.justification: Section 7 and the full reference list are unchanged after matching entries across page breaks. The positioning relative to LiPO and earlier IR and alignment methods is retained.

P1.justification: The conclusion is rewritten, an acknowledgements section is added, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The remaining prose and the organization of the main text and appendices are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–7 retain their designs and placements. Minor footer-spacing changes accompany reference reflow: references now end on page 16, and acknowledgements occupy page 17.

improvement.justification: V1's conclusion describes an unrelated RAG study unsupported by the rest of the paper. V2 replaces it with a conclusion consistent with LarPO's methods and experiments, resolving a misleading internal inconsistency. The added acknowledgements improve attribution, while the scientific methods, proofs and experimental evidence remain unchanged.
